statement: For every prime p >= 11 and every integer 3 <= ell <= (p-3)/2, every ordered pair (A,B) of subsets of F_p with |B|=ell, |A|=p-ell, and |A dotplus B|=p-2 is simultaneously affinely equivalent to (A_(a,b),B_(a,b)) for some nonnegative a,b with a+b=ell, with B_(a,b)={-2j:0<=j<a} union {1+2j:0<=j<b}, C_(a,b)={2+2j:0<=j<a} union {-1-2j:0<=j<b}, and A_(a,b)=F_p minus C_(a,b). Every displayed pair has missing restricted sums exactly {0,2}. Two displayed representatives are affinely equivalent if and only if (a,b) agrees up to swapping, so there are floor(ell/2)+1 affine classes.
contribution: A complete elementary proof of the frozen classification. Its decisive ingredient is an exact endpoint-corrected count of cyclic +2-runs, which also supplies the modular no-wrap argument; the proof includes a direct converse and affine-uniqueness analysis. No priority or novelty claim is made because full overlap checking against the closed-access Liu-Qian article remains unavailable.
